title: A smile aimed at getting attention is listed at 4 months
summary: Most children smile on their own to get a caregiver's attention by about 4 months, CDC says.
body: On the 4-month social list, CDC includes smiling on his own to get your attention, and chuckling, not yet a full laugh, when you try to make him laugh. The page's most means 75 percent or more of children, not every child. A smile used to draw someone in is a social bid. The checklist is not a diagnosis, and the page says the materials do not replace a validated screen. Ages on lists outside the United States can differ.
